body.estimand_functional: \(\tau_P(x)=\lim_{z\to x,z\in A_1}E_{P^{\mathrm{obs}}}[Y\mid X=z,T=1]-\lim_{z\to x,z\in A_0}E_{P^{\mathrm{obs}}}[Y\mid X=z,T=0]\)

sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from a causal law with sharp flat-boundary assignment; only the observed law is available.
sampling_model.overlap: There is no treatment overlap at a fixed score. For each \(x\in B\), the lower side-mass bound puts \(x\) in the support of both restricted score laws. Sharp assignment and consistency make the observed side regression equal to \(m_{t,P}\) almost everywhere on side \(t\); the declared Lipschitz representative is continuous and unique on that support. Therefore its observed-side limit at \(x\) equals \(\theta_{t,P}(x)\), and subtracting the two limits identifies \(\tau_P(x)=\theta_{1,P}(x)-\theta_{0,P}(x)\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: First-half scores determine a fully explicit finite grid and estimate masses and packing counts; total clipped second-half side averages estimate the traces. Neither \(\kappa\), the density, nor the profile class is estimated parametrically.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The pointwise minimax rate is derived for a univariate regularly varying design at a degenerate target; neither class inclusion nor direct theorem transfer is asserted here.
The paper studies pointwise adaptation in a univariate inhomogeneous design; its logarithmic lower bound concerns smoothness adaptation, whereas \(L\) is fixed in the present model.
The uniform results use a univariate design with finitely many zeros and a spatially normalized loss; neither class inclusion nor direct theorem transfer is asserted here.
The exact supremum-norm benchmark assumes a design density with a positive minimum and informs only the regular-design specialization.
The submanifold-integral minimax rate assumes design density bounded above and away from zero and concerns a scalar integral rather than a boundary trace.

The location-based class assumes a continuous score density bounded away from zero, smoother conditional means, and finite \(2+\nu\) moments; the regular corollary is compared only on its sub-Gaussian overlap with the present model.

The distance-based isotropic result is stated on a positive-density smooth boundary class; it does not transfer to the larger vanishing-density class, and any estimator-restricted converse remains estimator-restricted.

body.tldr: A single total measurable split-sample estimator adapts to thin-site multiplicity along an identified causal boundary trace. The empirical packing count now has a proved same-radius upper comparison: equation \(a_P(g,h)\leq a^U(g,h)\) and odd/even splitting yield \(\widehat J(h,v)\leq C\{1\vee J_P(h,C(v+\log(en)/n_1))\}\). A precise multiscale selected-interval forest proves the varying-bandwidth stochastic bound without paying for all radii or severity layers. The resulting oracle gives the isolated rate \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\), the pervasive rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\), and, under quadratic side mass, the regular rate \((\log n/n)^{1/4}\) for the same procedure.

project_justification.gap: Degenerate-design theory treats univariate regularly varying designs or finitely many zeros under pointwise or spatially normalized loss, while positive-density boundary theory does not cover polynomially vanishing side mass. Neither supplies a measurable same-radius packing oracle for a sample-selected boundary bandwidth.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a profile-adaptive estimator whose penalty uses \(1+\log\{e(1\vee J_P(h,u))\}\) at the estimator's own radius and local severity, together with a multiscale argument that does not insert a global radius-count penalty.
project_justification.fill: The project proves a tie-safe source-labeled pattern representative, the same-radius empirical packing comparison by direct odd/even splitting, and an explicit interval-forest charge for selected radii. These results yield regular, isolated, and pervasive guarantees for one total estimator, with empty counts and empty admissible sets handled explicitly.

body.related_work: Gaiffas (2005) studies pointwise rates for univariate regularly varying designs. Gaiffas (2007) studies pointwise smoothness adaptation; its logarithmic lower bound concerns adaptation over smoothness, whereas the present \(L\) is fixed. Gaiffas (2009) treats univariate inhomogeneous designs with finitely many zeros and spatially normalized uniform loss. Those classes are neither asserted to contain nor to be contained in the present two-sided boundary profile classes, so no theorem is transferred directly. Antoniadis, Pensky, and Sapatinas (2014) likewise study global adaptation in a univariate inhomogeneous design, and Bertin (2004) supplies a positive-density supremum benchmark. Chen and Gao (2026) concern scalar submanifold integrals under positive bounded design density, not an entire depleted boundary trace. Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu impose continuous density bounded away from zero, smoother conditional means, and finite \(2+\nu\) moments. The regular-design corollary is identified only with the sub-Gaussian overlap of their positive-density class; their upper results do not transfer to the larger vanishing-density class. Likewise, a converse restricted to a specified estimator or decision class remains estimator-restricted and is not used as an unrestricted minimax converse here. The new component is the same-radius protected packing oracle and its multiscale selected-bandwidth proof.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Scalar side mass does not imply coercivity of higher-order local-polynomial Gram matrices, so the estimator uses local averages. It treats \(L\) and \(\sigma\) as fixed known class constants. Constants are uniform only on compact exponent sets bounded away from \(2\). The regular-design comparison covers only laws satisfying the present conditional sub-Gaussian condition as well as quadratic one-sided mass; it is not a claim about the full positive-density comparator class.
body.honest_scope: The closed novelty claim is the same-radius profile-packing oracle inequality, including the multiscale selected-interval bound that removes the informal varying-bandwidth charge. The unit floor \(1\vee J_P\) is retained everywhere because \(\widehat J\geq1\) even for an empty population thin set; it contributes only a numerical constant. The same total estimator attains the regular \((\log n/n)^{1/4}\), isolated \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\), and pervasive \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\) upper rates under their stated law conditions. Identification is a supporting observed-law argument, not the headline. The endpoint minimax orders remain attributed to the banked parent result. No arbitrary-profile exactness, local-oracle band claim, transfer from a full Cattaneo--Titiunik--Yu class, or unrestricted use of an estimator-restricted converse is asserted.
